speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether Changi Airport is vulnerable to disruptions caused by drones similar to those at London's Gatwick Airport and, if so, to what extent.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: asked the Minister for Transport what measures does the Government have against drones or other unmanned aerial devices that may disrupt flight operations in and around airports in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Transport what measures are in place to prevent or stop drones from operating in the vicinity of our airports and affecting flight operations and schedules.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Minister for Transport what are the measures to ensure that flying drones does not disrupt the air traffic around Changi Airport.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, we recognise the need to address safety and security concerns that could arise from errant and irresponsible use of UAS.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These efforts are coordinated with the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, due to security considerations, it would not be appropriate for me to go into the details.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will continue to monitor developments globally and collaborate with foreign counterparts and industry partners to study and implement additional measures when required.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Learning from the Gatwick Airport incident, I think there were two issues, and I would like to pose two supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: And how can they disrupt the operation of rogue drones?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They are very pertinent to the safety and the security of our aerodromes.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Of course, the Auxiliary Police Officers would also be activated to respond if air traffic controller or pilots of aircraft report sightings of such activities.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the Member's supplementary question on the efforts to neutralise rogue UAS, CAAS' approach is to consider both cooperative as well as uncooperative UAS.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As for uncooperative UAS, CAAS actually collaborates with Changi Airport Group, Defence Science and Technology Agency, MINDEF as well as MHA to neutralise either by forcing down or destroying rogue UAS swiftly, but such counter UAS technology or solutions are classified and, for security reasons, I am afraid I would not be able to go into the details on it.
